Son cheval fu tant traveillies qu’il ne pout plus, e fu noiez Batho, e grant partie de ses genz dedeins le flume avant que poissent venir a l’autre rive. Quant les Tartars, qui encore n’estoient entrez en l’eive, virent leur seignor Batho e leur compaignies noier, dolens e tristes s’en retournerent au roiaume de Roussie e de Comaine, ne onques puis les Tartars n’entrerent en Alemaigne. — Hayton of Corycus , in: La Flor des estoires de la terre d'Orient His horse was so exhausted that it could not continue, and Batu was drowned with a great number of his people in the river before they could reach the other bank. When the Tartars who had not yet entered the water saw their lord Batu and their companions drown, they returned mournfully and sadly to the kingdom of Russia and of Cumania; never again did the Tartars invade Germany — trans. Pow, Stephen, "Later Rumors of Mongol Defeat in Europe in the Mid-Thirteenth Century: Batu's Drowning in Austria and the Saint Ladislaus Legend in Russia." Vestnik of Saint Petersburg University History , vol. 70, No. 1, April 2025, pp. 9–10.

kandidater.beskrivning: Mentions not receiving his salary checks in the mail. Includes envelope. Transcription: The American Women's Club. 46, Grosvenor Street. W.1. Letter No. 18. 33. Sept. 18, '23. Your cable just rec'd. Have plenty of money. My idea was not to lose the 2 checks. Dearest Boy: I do long for my darling especially to-day, for the my cold, that has been advancing and retreating for 10 days seems to-day to have defeated me utterly in a pitched battle. I am laid up, in plain English. This changeable chilly weather with a chilly house to live in have done it, I suppose. I felt Sunday and Monday (yesterday) that the medicine and gargles and sprays had got rid of it for me — but when I woke at about 4:00 this morning I saw it had redeveloped over night. So I am staying in my room today and am having my dinner brought up. Why the thing should have descended I don't know, for I had a very easy day yesterday — that I is, I was alone all day and went to the Nat'l Gallery again in the morning. It was a glorious hour and a half I spent there — but I suppose the chilly rooms got in their work. But I did have a beautiful morning. What a splendor [Diego] Valasquez's "Rokeby Venus" is! Do you remember it? The salary check for Sept. 1 not having reached me, I wonder if [G.R.] Hoare's man has redirected the letter to you by mistake? My Guaranty Trust Co. check also sent to Hoare has not reached me either. Both are overdue. I telephoned the Guaranty this morning and after much delay they said that the duplicate of my check had reached them, showing beyond a doubt that the original was mailed to me here to London as usual. But they will not cash the duplicate. I do not know what to do about these checks. I phoned Hoare's office and they declare they have mailed my mail here. I therefore sent you the following cable: Filsinger Care Grand Hotel Stockholm. Your salary my check not received. Were they sent you? Shall I have payment stopped on these checks? The clocks have been put back an hour and it is pitch dark now a few minutes after seven. The autumn is on us. Just now came some lovely yellow roses and a package of books from Staf [Henry Stafford Hatfield]. Your letter of Sept. 12 from Helsingfors [Helsinki] came this morning. How glad I was to see your writing as I got up, feeling rocky with my cold. How fine to see again in this letter your pleasure in your trip to Russia! My summer too would have been a perfect one (as earthly things go) except for this cold. If I had realized I'd be taken ill, I'd have gone home alone on Sept. 8, and so have escaped. Ah well. I know that my beloved has his hands full hurrying to get here in time to sail. May all go well with my darling. Tragic about the Abbotts! I phoned Bumpus' about sending you the book. It took ages and the man finally agreed that he couldn't understand over the 'phone, so he sent over a message and I wrote it all out in a note. I hope the book reaches you. I was not well enough to go after it. Love. Kisses Your Sara.

kandidater.beskrivning: Kalmar Castle is a fortified castle in Kalmar, on the Strait of Kalmar in south-eastern Sweden. History: The castle was first built by King Magnus Ladulås. It was later upgraded to the time of the Vasa by Eric XIV and his brother John III who made the castle a medieval palace fit for a king at the time of the Renaissance. This castle played an important role in the history of Sweden. Thus, it is here that in 1397 the treaty of the three Scandinavian kingdoms (Denmark, Norway, Sweden) establishing the Kalmar Union under one ruler was signed: Eric of Pomerania, nephew of Queen Marguerite Ire of Denmark at the time was the real ruler of the Scandinavian countries. Architecture: restoration of the castle in the nineteenth century. In 1856, the architect Fredrik Wilhelm Scholander (1816-1881) began restoration work in Kalmar, pursued by his pupil Helgo Zettervall (1885-1891): this work gives the castle its current form. In 1919, Professor Martin Olsson is responsible for the result of restoration work (earthworks, moats and drawbridges Bridge) in 1941, the castle was again surrounded by water. The castle is now under protection and is accessible to the public.
